t: Subject scoping from a seed description (foundational)
title: Subject scoping from a seed description (foundational)
description: Signature original: The new subject starts from a seed description that is expanded into a scope: core topics in, adjacent topics parked, explicit exclusions. Scoping prevents the knowledge base from sprawling into neighboring subjects. The scope document is reviewed before any corpus assembly begins. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Knowledge Base Generator, 2026-10-21.

title: Corpus assembly from approved sources (foundational)
description: Signature original: Source documents are gathered from the archive's approved collections matching the scope, with provenance recorded per document. Assembly favors primary sources and recent material, and deduplicates near-identical documents. The corpus is the knowledge base's raw material; its quality bounds everything built on it. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

title: Topic clustering of the corpus (foundational)
description: Signature original: Documents are clustered by term overlap into topic groups, giving the knowledge base its browse structure. Clustering uses agglomerative merging on Jaccard similarity with a similarity floor, which needs no predeclared cluster count. Each cluster is labeled by its most distinctive terms. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Knowledge Base Generator, 2026-10-21.

t: Search index construction over the corpus (foundational)
title: Search index construction over the corpus (foundational)
description: Signature original: An inverted index is built over the corpus: each term maps to the documents containing it with positions. The index makes the knowledge base searchable from the moment it is published. Construction is a single pass over the corpus, linear in total text length. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Knowledge Base Generator, 2026-10-21.

title: Question-answering smoke test (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before publication, the knowledge base answers a smoke-test set of questions drawn from its scope, and each answer is checked for support in the corpus. The smoke test catches empty clusters, broken indexes, and scope drift. A knowledge base that fails smoke testing does not ship. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
qa = [('what maps terms to docs?', 'inverted index'), ('what stores positions?', 'posting lists')]
corpus_text = 'inverted index maps terms to docs. posting lists store positions.'
passed = sum(1 for q, a in qa if a in corpus_text)
print(f'smoke test: {passed}/{len(qa)} passed')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Automatic Knowledge Base Generator, 2026-10-21.
